proofs.requirement: Myoepithelial cells are living nucleated cells; the extracellular basement membrane is distinct from those cells and from their plasma membranes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. Myoepithelial cells have contractile features that help move milk; they are not the chest muscle. Basement membrane contains matrix proteins such as laminins and type IV collagen, not living cells.

Basement membrane beneath an epithelial structure differs from plasma membrane around one cell. Cell polarity describes different inward and outward organisation. Gudjonsson and colleagues' human-cell culture experiments showed that normal myoepithelial cells or laminin-1 could restore luminal orientation in collagen gels; this is model evidence about organisation, not a demonstrated cancer treatment.
